title: Keeping in Place After the Storm-Emergency Assistance and Evictions
abstract: arXiv:2505.14548v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We offer evidence that federal emergency assistance (FEMA) in the days following natural disasters mitigate evictions in comparison to similar emergency scenarios where FEMA aid is not provided. We find an approximate 10.9% increase in overall evictions after hurricane natural disaster events driven in large part by areas in close proximity of the hurricane path that do not receive FEMA rental assistance. Furthermore, we also show that FEMA aid acts as a liquidity buffer to other forms of emergency credit, specifically we find that overall transactions volumes decrease during hurricane events in locations that do receive FEMA aid. This effect largely reverses in areas that do not receive FEMA aid. translated_title: 《风暴过后安居原地——紧急援助与驱逐》
translated_abstract: 本文提供了证据表明，在自然灾害发生后的几天内，联邦紧急事务管理局（FEMA）的紧急援助相比未提供FEMA援助的类似紧急情况，能够缓解驱逐事件的发生。我们发现，飓风自然灾害事件后，总体驱逐率上升约10.9%，这在很大程度上是由飓风路径附近未获得FEMA租金援助的地区所驱动的。此外，我们还表明，FEMA援助对其他形式的紧急信贷起到流动性缓冲作用——具体而言，我们发现接受FEMA援助的地区在飓风事件期间整体交易量有所下降，而在未接受FEMA援助的地区，这一效应基本发生逆转。总体而言，这表明自然灾害事件期间紧急流动性的可得性确实是一个具有约束力的限制条件，会对家庭财务产生实际影响，特别是通过本文所记录的驱逐渠道等途径体现。
tldr: 本文发现FEMA紧急援助能显著缓解飓风灾害后的驱逐问题——未获得FEMA租金援助的飓风路径附近地区驱逐率上升约10.9%，证明灾害期间的紧急流动性供给是影响家庭财务稳定的关键约束。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that FEMA emergency assistance mitigates post-disaster evictions—areas near hurricane paths without FEMA rental aid experience a ~10.9% increase in evictions, demonstrating that emergency liquidity availability is a binding constraint with real household financial consequences.
